gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that Apple splits the 16-inch MacBook Pro by model year for 140 W charging: the Nov 2023 and later models take it over a 240 W USB-C cable (the kind UGREEN ships with its 48,000 mAh bank, per Macworld), while earlier 16-inch models need Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable. None states either that on the CUKTECH 30 only USB-C2 offers 28 V/5 A.
standout_why: Compared against four results. Macworld's UGREEN 48000mAh review (2024-07-17) already says the shipped cable is 240 W-capable and that Apple requires its MagSafe 3 cable for 140 W; it lacks the Nov 2023 split now on Apple's page. Macworld's roundup gives the UGREEN per-port ratings (140 W PD 3.1 on one USB-C, 100 W PD 3.0 on two) but no cable-by-model cell. powerbanks.fyi (cited) lists the CUKTECH 30 and UGREEN 48,000 with per-port wattage 'not stated' and nothing on cables or laptop models. Tom's Guide (cited) returned only navigation and deals text to my fetch, so I could not compare it. I did not open Wired, Digital Camera World, solargenadvisor, best-batteries or the other results.
decides: It confirms the picks rather than changing them. Both 140 W banks (UGREEN 48,000 mAh at $118.99, AOHi Starship 40K) can fast-charge a 16-inch MacBook Pro, but a pre-Nov-2023 model needs Apple's MagSafe 3 cable, which neither box is shown to include. A 14-inch MacBook Pro or 2022+ MacBook Air fast-charges from 96 W or 70 W, so a 100 W port already covers them. ChatGPT's first pick, the CUKTECH 30, is not orderable at its maker's store today ($999.00 placeholder, unavailable), and ChargerLab found PD 3.1 only on its USB-C2. That favors UGREEN as the buyable 140 W pick and AOHi as the exact-40,000 mAh one.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro: adapter and cable Apple lists for fast charging
findings.value: 140 W USB-C adapter with USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable (16-inch, 2021 or later); 140 W adapter with 240W USB-C Charge Cable only for '16-inch, Nov 2023' or later
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple page dated 2026-11-05. Apple writes about its own adapter and cables; applying it to a power bank's 140 W PD 3.1 port is our reading. The page does not say which Mac port each cable plugs into.

findings.label: 14-inch MacBook Pro and MacBook Air: wattage Apple lists for fast charging
findings.value: 14-inch MacBook Pro (2021 or later): 96 W or 140 W adapter with MagSafe 3 or USB-C charge cable. MacBook Air (2022 or later): 70 W, 96 W or 140 W adapter with either cable; 67 W applies to 13.6-inch models only
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: So a 100 W USB-C port meets Apple's fast-charge wattage for these models; only the 16-inch needs 140 W (PD 3.1).

findings.label: Cable in the box
findings.value: 240 W-capable USB-C cable; no built-in cable
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review: more power and ports than most | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: 'The charging cable that ships with the power bank is capable of 240W.' Review dated 2024-07-17. Its line that Apple requires MagSafe 3 rather than USB-C for 140 W predates the Nov 2023 entry on Apple's page. UGREEN's own box contents were not read (store returned HTTP 429).

findings.label: Which port gives what
findings.value: USB-C1 140 W (PD 3.1); the other two USB-C 100 W each (PD 3.0); 2x USB-A 22.5 W; 300 W total; input 140 W
findings.source_title: Best laptop power banks for Apple MacBook 2026 | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld's spec line, page dated 2026-11-04. Its review adds that the first USB-C is the 140 W one, that all three USB-C cannot run at full power together (three at 100 W, or one 140 W plus one 100 W plus lower-power devices), and that recharge takes about 1.5 h through the 140 W port. Macworld also lists 48,000 mAh (153.6 Wh), 3.6 lb (1.65 kg) and 'airline: yes (with carrier approval)'.

findings.source_title: UGREEN Portable Power Station 48000mAh 300W with Smart Digital Display – UGREEN US
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search on us.ugreen.com (the store's search listing for this URL). The product page itself returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so no variant-level or sale-end detail was read.

findings.label: Price and listings at AOHi's store
findings.value: Base listing $179.00, list $259.00, in stock (title: '[Black Friday Deals $143]'). Separate listing 'with 240W 3FT C-C Cable' $179.99, list $259.00, in stock
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py search on iaohi.com; the product page returned HTTP 429. The cable listing is https://iaohi.com/products/aohi-starship-2-in-1-40000mah-140w-power-bank-power-station.

findings.label: Port count as AOHi words it (inconsistent)
findings.value: Base listing: 'three USB-C 140W ports and one USB-A port', 'charge up to three devices at once'. Bundle listings: 'two USB-C 140W output ports and one USB-A port'
findings.note: AOHi's listing copy via the store search. Our record says two 140 W outputs plus one 140 W input, which matches the 'two output ports' wording; the page should not repeat 'three 140W ports' as three outputs. AOHi also states PD 3.1 140 W, MacBook Pro 16-inch 0 to 56% in 30 minutes, and 2.09 x 2.56 x 6.77 in. The cable listing says that with a 140 W input connected it charges itself and three devices.

findings.label: Which USB-C port carries PD 3.1
findings.value: USB-C2 offers 20 V and 28 V at 5 A (28 V x 5 A = 140 W); USB-C1 stops at 20 V/5 A (100 W)
findings.source_title: Teardown of CUKTECH No.30 PD3.1 & 300W Power Bank (P01CT) - ChargerLAB
findings.note: ChargerLAB (Joey, 2023-07-03) protocol readings on model P01CT; the 140 W and 100 W figures are our arithmetic from its voltage and current lists. It also gives a 141 Wh label rating, about 1.13 kg and 300 W total. CUKTECH's own spec table was not read (HTTP 429), and the US unit Best Buy lists as PB01CT may differ.

findings.label: What the cited spec-list page gives for these two banks
findings.value: CUKTECH 30: 40,000 mAh / 144 Wh, 1,130 g, 300 W, price unavailable. UGREEN 48,000: 153.6 Wh, 1,637 g, 300 W, $169.99. No per-port wattage, cable or laptop-model detail for either
